name: St. Henry's Ecumenical Art Chapel
key_features: Copper-clad, boat-shaped chapel on a rocky ridge, with a pine-ribbed interior like an upturned hull.

name: Gothenburg Law Courts Extension
key_features: A restrained new wing beside the old courthouse, around a top-lit, timber-lined atrium of stairs and galleries.

name: Hornbækhus
key_features: A whole city block of brick flats, identical windows repeated without a break around one big green court.

name: Nordic House in the Faroe Islands
key_features: A turf-roofed cultural centre like a hill of elves, its glass walls braced by steel struts against hurricane winds.

name: Powerhouse Brattørkaia
key_features: Energy-positive office: a dark wedge whose steep roof is one big solar array, cut by an oval courtyard.

name: St. Hallvard Church and Monastery
key_features: A square brick block outside, a round church within, under a concrete ceiling that sags down like a bowl.

name: The Twist
key_features: Gallery, bridge and sculpture in one: an aluminium-clad box that turns 90° as it spans 60 m over the river.

name: Wadden Sea Centre
key_features: Low visitor centre on the marsh whose thatch runs over the roof and down the walls, in long sloping planes.

name: Kela Main Office (National Pensions Institute)
key_features: Red-brick and copper office block stepped round a raised courtyard, with a top-lit main hall inside.

name: Fragrant Hill Hotel
key_features: White walls with grey trim and diamond-patterned openings that frame garden views, after Suzhou houses.

name: National Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
key_features: Modern hall under a sweeping roof of yellow glazed tiles with upturned corners, a palace-style touch Chiang asked for.

name: National Palace Museum
key_features: Palace-style museum set against a hill: green-tiled roofs, yellow walls and white stairs on a long axis.

name: Ordos Museum
key_features: Rounded, edgeless shell wrapped in polished metal louvres, its form drawn from the Gobi Desert.

name: Peace Hotel (Sassoon House)
key_features: Granite-faced Art Deco block on the Bund, topped by a steep copper pyramid roof gone green.

name: Ningbo Museum of Art
key_features: Long grey-brick plinth carrying a timber-slatted steel box, reached by bridges across a moat.

name: Xiqu Centre
by: Revery Architecture, Ronald Lu and Partners
key_features: Chinese opera house wrapped in a curved skin of fins, its corners pulled open like a stage curtain.

name: Hong Kong Cultural Centre
key_features: Windowless pink-tiled arts centre on the old railway station site, next to the surviving clock tower.

name: Kaohsiung Music Center
key_features: Harbourfront music venues: two towers of stacked hexagonal lattice cells beside a low faceted hall.

name: Water-Moon Monastery (Nung Chan Monastery)
key_features: Long fair-faced concrete hall raised on columns, its screen wall pierced with scripture characters.

name: Taipei Music Center
key_features: Concert hall under a folded, crystalline metal roof, set apart from a cultural hall and production wing.

name: Shanghai Museum
key_features: Shaped like an ancient bronze ding: a round top over a square base, for round sky and square earth.

name: Tianjin Binhai Library
by: MVRDV, Tianjin Urban Planning and Design Institute
key_features: Terraced white shelves wave up the atrium around a luminous sphere, seen from the park through an eye-shaped opening.

name: Tao Zhu Yin Yuan
key_features: 21-storey tower twisting 90 degrees like a DNA double helix, each floor turned 4.5 degrees, planted with trees.

name: Wah Fu Estate
key_features: Public housing planned as a self-contained new town by the sea, with its own shops and bus terminus.

name: Zhongshan Hall (Taipei Public Hall)
key_features: Steel-framed hall built to resist fire, quakes and typhoons, faced in green tile, with Islamic-style windows.

name: Shanghai Oriental Art Center
key_features: Five linked glass-walled halls like petals; from above the plan reads as a butterfly orchid.

name: College of Social Sciences, National Taiwan University (Koo Chen-Fu Memorial Library)
key_features: Single-storey glazed reading room under a skylit roof held up by 88 tree-like columns.

name: Forbidden City
key_features: Walled and moated palace city of 980 buildings strung along Beijing's north-south axis.

name: Prime Tower
key_features: 126 m green-glass office tower whose irregular octagonal plan steps out in two places as it rises.

name: Kirchner Museum Davos
key_features: Four glass-clad gallery cubes linked by a lower corridor; daylight reaches the rooms from above through etched glass.

name: German Maritime Museum (Scharoun building)
key_features: Finished after Scharoun's death: a ship-like building with railing-style balconies, beside a fleet of museum ships.

name: Kunstmuseum Basel, New Building
key_features: Angular block faced in grey concrete bricks, kept to the old museum's height; a lettering frieze is set into the wall.

name: Museum Brandhorst
key_features: Facade of 36,000 vertical ceramic louvres in 23 coloured glazes that blend into one shimmering surface from afar.

name: GSW Headquarters
key_features: Thin curved slab added to a 1950s tower; its west double facade of pink and orange shading panels ventilates it.

name: Tour Total (Jean-Monnet-Tower)
key_features: 69 m office tower wrapped in a load-bearing grid of faceted precast-concrete elements that shade its glass.

name: Museum der bildenden Künste, Leipzig
by: Hufnagel Pütz Rafaelian (Karl Hufnagel, Peter Pütz, Michael Rafaelian)
key_features: Glass-clad box on a former city square, framed by lower corner buildings that rebuild the old street block.

name: Kant-Dreieck
key_features: 11-storey tower, a steel cube on a stone base, crowned by a huge sheet-metal 'sail' that turns in the wind.

name: Norddeutsche Landesbank (NORD/LB) Headquarters
key_features: Glass perimeter block around a planted court, with a tower of glass boxes stacked and twisted off a central core.

name: Kunstmuseum Bonn
key_features: Exposed-concrete galleries with a big roofed outdoor area on slim round columns, behind a tall 13 m wall.

name: Zentralsparkasse Branch, Favoritenstrasse
key_features: Bank front of bulging, rippling steel panels between plain houses; inside, a giant concrete hand holds the stair.

name: Loisium Wine World
key_features: Aluminium-clad cube sliced by window cuts that trace the old wine cellar tunnels, which visitors walk into.

name: Kaufhaus Tyrol
key_features: Store front in three slightly angled sections of deep-set columns in white stone-aggregate concrete.

name: Lentos Art Museum
key_features: 130 m glass-skinned box on the Danube that glows in changing colours at night, with a large opening to the river.

name: Wiener Stadthalle
key_features: Austria's largest indoor arena, its roof held up by a tension band above raking grandstand supports.

name: Werkraum Haus
key_features: Showroom for the Bregenzerwald craftsmen's guild: one big roof on slim pillars over a glass-walled hall.

name: LifeCycle Tower One (LCT ONE)
key_features: Eight-storey timber high-rise prototype: prefab timber-concrete floors round a concrete core, raised in eight days.

name: Frauenmuseum Hittisau
key_features: A plain timber-clad village box with one big glazed front, holding a women's museum above the local fire station.

name: Joan Miró's Studio (Taller Sert)
key_features: Painter's studio under a row of wave-shaped concrete vaults that bring daylight deep into the workspace.

name: Torres de Colón
key_features: Twin office towers whose floors hang from the tops of their concrete cores ("suspended architecture").

name: Museum of Memory of Andalusia (MA)
key_features: Long white podium cut by an elliptical courtyard whose ramps spiral between the floors.

name: Royal Collections Gallery
by: Mansilla + Tuñón (Luis Moreno Mansilla, Emilio Tuñón)
key_features: Museum dug into the slope below the Royal Palace, its long facade a rhythm of pale vertical piers.

name: Museu de Belles Arts de Castelló
key_features: Metal-clad gallery block whose stepped rooftop lanterns light the rooms, joined to an older building around a patio.

name: Seville–Santa Justa Station
key_features: Brick station under a long curved concrete canopy, opening onto a high vaulted platform hall.

name: La Ricarda (Casa Gomis)
key_features: Pavilion house of thin concrete vaults on a modular grid, spread among pine trees near the sea.

name: Pavilion of Knowledge (Pavilhão do Conhecimento)
key_features: White science museum around an open patio, its long upper block cantilevered over the court.

name: Nadir Afonso Contemporary Art Museum
key_features: Long white concrete museum lifted on piers above the riverside meadow.

name: Setúbal School of Education
key_features: Low white school around a U-shaped lawn, lined by a deep colonnade.

name: Matosinhos Town Hall
key_features: Stone-clad town hall with long colonnades, set back behind a row of poplars on a civic square.

name: Metropolitano Stadium
key_features: Stadium built around a 1994 stand, now under a single tensile roof ring wrapping all four sides.

name: Grosvenor Place
key_features: 44-storey tower with column-free 2,000 m² floors; a diagonal walk passes two kept heritage buildings.

name: QV1
key_features: 40-storey tower with sunshades over its windows; free curving plaza buildings offset its strict geometry.

name: Featherston House
key_features: One glass-walled room over an indoor garden, with platforms floating off the central chimney like a treehouse.

name: Riverside Centre
key_features: 40-storey office tower above an open riverfront plaza with steps, cafés and a ferry wharf.

name: Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law
key_features: Supreme and District Court tower that, with the Magistrates Court, fills a city block as a legal precinct.

name: RMIT Design Hub
by: Sean Godsell Architects with Peddle Thorp
key_features: Skin of sandblasted glass discs that a computer turns to control sun and heat, like a second wall.

name: Swanston Academic Building (RMIT Building 80)
key_features: 11-storey teaching block wrapped in angled coloured panels meant to wear the 'cloak' of the city around it.

name: Melbourne School of Design (Glyn Davis Building)
key_features: Architecture school built as a teaching tool: exposed structure and a studio hall under a coffered timber roof.

name: Ian Potter Museum of Art
key_features: University art museum whose grey street wall carries a frieze of broken classical fragments.

name: Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies
key_features: Waterfront research 'shed' on Princes Wharf, its long folded roof lifting into a glazed end towards the harbour.

name: Wellington Central Library (Te Matapihi)
key_features: Library on Civic Square with a curving glass wall behind a colonnade of metal nīkau-palm columns.

name: Palmerston North City Library
key_features: Old department store on The Square restored and extended as the city library, with angled steel and glass additions.

name: Art Gallery of New South Wales, North Building (Sydney Modern, Naala Nura)
key_features: Glass pavilions under thin roofs step down to Woolloomooloo Bay; a disused oil tank below became 'The Tank' gallery.

name: Melbourne Recital Centre
key_features: Concert hall with a cell-like glass and panel facade, holding a 1,000-seat 'modified shoebox' hall.

name: Melbourne Museum
key_features: Two long sloping roof blades rise over the entrance, on axis with the 1880 Royal Exhibition Building opposite.

name: Michael Fowler Centre
by: Warren and Mahoney (Miles Warren, Maurice Mahoney)
key_features: Concert hall of tilted concrete panels over a glass circulation band, nicknamed the 'Squashed Top Hat'.

name: Sky Tower
key_features: 328 m concrete telecom and observation tower whose shaft stands on eight legs, with a revolving restaurant at 190 m.

name: Governor Phillip Tower
key_features: Granite and glass tower raised on zinc-plated beams over a sandstone podium, crowned by a steel 'milk-crate'.

name: Tūranga (Christchurch Central Library)
key_features: Post-earthquake central library on Cathedral Square, partly wrapped in a golden screen inspired by the Port Hills.

name: University House, Australian National University
key_features: ANU's first residential college: long low wings and covered walkways round a courtyard with a pond.

name: ICI House (Orica House)
key_features: Australia's first International Style skyscraper, an all-glass slab that broke Melbourne's 132 ft height limit.

name: Qantas House (No. 1 Chifley Square)
key_features: Segmented curved curtain wall of green glass and blue-green spandrels that shapes the edge of Chifley Square.

name: Green Square Library and Plaza
key_features: Library sunk below a public plaza; only a glass tower, a triangular skylight and sunken garden rise above ground.

name: National Library of Australia
key_features: Stripped Classical library on Lake Burley Griffin: a colonnade of slim columns under a flat roof, marble foyer inside.

name: Eureka Tower
key_features: 91-storey apartment tower themed on the Eureka Stockade: blue glass for the flag, a gold crown and a red stripe.

name: Rialto Towers
by: Gerard de Preu and Partners with Perrott Lyon Mathieson
key_features: Two conjoined towers (43 and 55 floors) in blue mirror glass that turns gold at sunset.

name: Te Uru Waitākere Contemporary Gallery
key_features: Green-clad gallery beside the old Lopdell House in the bush suburb of Titirangi, with bright orange entry panels.

name: Sydney Tower (Centrepoint Tower)
key_features: 309 m observation tower: a golden turret on a slender shaft, rising from a shopping-centre podium.

name: Southern Cross Station
key_features: Wave-shaped roof on branching steel columns spans the whole station block, the city's main rail and coach hub.

name: University of Warsaw Library (BUW)
key_features: Library with one of Europe's largest public roof gardens, designed by Irena Bajerska; opened 15 December 1999.

name: Legiobanka (Bank of the Czechoslovak Legions)
key_features: Head office of the Legion Bank; its style gave Czech Art Deco ('rondocubism') the name 'Legiobank style'.

name: Hotel Intercontinental Prague (Fairmont Golden Prague)
key_features: Brutalist riverside hotel by a team led by Karel Filsak; exposed concrete and a ceramic façade, restored in 2021–25.

name: Hôtel de Ville, Le Havre
key_features: 70 m, 18-storey reinforced-concrete tower at one end of a 143 m block with a 15-bay colonnaded facade.

name: Tour Montparnasse
by: Eugène Beaudouin, Urbain Cassan, Louis de Hoÿm de Marien
key_features: 210 m glass-and-steel tower on 56 concrete piles sunk 70 m, with a concrete shield protecting the Metro below.

name: Stade de France
by: Michel Macary, Aymeric Zublena, Michel Regembal, Claude Constantini
key_features: Elliptical roof of about six hectares and 13,000 t; a movable stand retracts to uncover the athletics track.

name: Palais de Chaillot
by: Louis-Hippolyte Boileau, Jacques Carlu, Léon Azéma
key_features: Two curved wings around a terrace that opens a view to the Eiffel Tower; facades carry Paul Valéry inscriptions.

name: Mobilier National
key_features: Perret's 1937 home of the state furniture workshops: concrete used with classical symmetry and proportion.

name: Station F (Halle Freyssinet)
key_features: 1929 rail freight depot by Freyssinet, turned into a startup campus of about 34,000 m² in 2017.

name: Passerelle Simone-de-Beauvoir
key_features: 304 m footbridge with a lens-shaped steel central span 106 m long and 650 t.

name: Halle Tony Garnier
key_features: Steel roof truss on ball-and-socket joints leaves the 80 x 210 m former cattle hall free of columns.

name: Hôtel du Département des Bouches-du-Rhône (Le Grand Bleu)
key_features: Blue-glass 'Grand Bleu' with a 'skin of art' by Brian Clarke, on X-shaped concrete pilotis; 80,000 m².
